content:
incident-bot: P1 detected — latency spike in us-east-1 hosted cluster. p95 went from ~420ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~3.6s. Affected model: redwood/rw-v2-large. Congestion signature: long tail on token generation (post-attention), noisy tenant correlation. Auto-throttle fired for some tenants.

alex: looking now. any recent rollouts to kernel selection or quant profiles?

maya: saw a small rollout this morning that enabled the new fused fast-attn kernel on rw-v2-large for batch size > 8. rollout id: rollout/2026-03-18-fastattn. Might be a mismatch with our batching distribution (most requests are small).

sam: infra shows node GPU busy but not fully saturated — lots of small inference jobs creating context switch overhead.

jordan: I can flip routing to route affected traffic to the stable kernel variant if we decide.

maya: profiler snapshot (top hotspots) — capturing flamegraph for a hot pod:
```text
top kernels by samples:
 fast_attn_kernel         46.3%  # increased since rollout
 matmul_opt               21.0%
 kv_cache_read            16.8%  # spikes on repeated prefix lookups
 other                    15.9%
```
Notice: fast_attn_kernel is dominating even when batch sizes are small -> higher per-token latency.

alex: that fits a kernel-selection mispredict: the selector is picking fast_attn based on microbenchmarks at larger batch sizes but our real workload is mostly batch 1-4.

kevin: what about KV cache behavior? any evictions causing rework?

maya: yes — KV cache miss rate for several tenants jumped from 2% -> 18% during spike window. We see lots of short-lived sessions that invalidate prefix caching; combined with kernel overhead, that pushes tail up.

tara: customer-facing alerter triggered. ETA for mitigation?

alex: propose immediate mitigations:
- enable feature flag to force stable kernel (safe/old path) for rw-v2-large in us-east-1
- enable per-tenant soft throttling for top noisy tenants (limit concurrency to 4)
- temporarily disable eager KV prefetch for hosted tier to reduce cache churn
Jordan can flip routing to fallback nodes if needed.

jordan: I can flip the kernel flag now. Preparing the feature flag: `ff set rwv2_force_stable_kernel=on --scope=us-east-1`

sam: spinning up extra warm pods would help throughput but might worsen noisy neighbor. I'd prefer routing + kernel fallback first.

incident-bot: Action logged: mitigation_attempt by jordan at 1891234523 — set rwv2_force_stable_kernel=on in us-east-1 (gradual rollout 10% -> 100%).

alex: rollback window ready. maya please monitor p95/p99 and KV miss rate.

maya: initial numbers after 10% rollout:
- p95: down to 1.2s (from 1.8s)
- p99: down to 2.4s (from 3.6s)
- KV miss rate: 14% -> 11%
Still elevated but trending.

jordan: increasing rollout to 50% now (1891234560).

incident-bot: Action logged: mitigation_progress — kernel fallback increased to 50% at 1891234560.

maya: after 50%:
- p95: ~650ms
- p99: ~1.1s
- KV miss: 9%
Looks much better.

tara: can we send a short customer note: "We saw elevated latencies in us-east, root cause kernel selection mismatch for one model. We applied fallback and are monitoring." Short, non-technical.

alex: good. I'll draft. Also open follow-ups: adjust kernel selector thresholds, add synthetic traffic tests for common small-batch mixes, tighten KV prefetch heuristics, and add an alert on kernel-sel mismatch.

kevin: created ticket PERF-1876: "Kernel selector policies: add batch-distribution-aware heuristics + KV churn safety" and assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://jira.internal.redwood/PROJ/PERF-1876

incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved at 1891234620 — mitigation succeeded, metrics within acceptable ranges. Postmortem assigned to maya + alex, due in 72h.

alex: thanks everyone. quick retro items: test rollout on small-batch workloads, add canary gate for kernel change when KV miss rate > 5%, and update runbook for noisy-tenant throttles.

maya: I'll grab the postmortem. uploading profiler dump and flamegraph to the incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/1891234500/flamegraph.svg

sam: leaving notes for infra: consider node-level p99 guardrails to prevent small-job context-switch storms.

jordan: closing channel for the incident, will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
